dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Hello. What are you looking at?

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Nothing much, really.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Just sitting here, listening to the sound of the water.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Do you come here every day?

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Ever since I was young, hearing this sound has always calmed me.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Did you see the surface of the Okawa River?

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Yes. The light reflecting off it was beautiful.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: That water surface looks different every day.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Every day? You mean it changes with the weather?

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Aye. It changes with the seasons, and with the time of day.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Though the water temperature stays right around 12°C, year in and year out.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Watch it long enough, and you'll start to understand how the water moves.

updateNotebook.memo: The water surface looks different every day. It changes with weather and seasons.
updateNotebook.quote: Watch it long enough, and you'll start to understand how the water moves.
updateNotebook.speaker: oldman

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Hearing the sound of the water just settles you right down, doesn't it.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Did you see the poster on the bulletin board?

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Yes. It's a festival called the Takashima Dance (高島踊り), right?

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: In the old days, the whole village would gather for this dance.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: When the dancing was over, everyone would share drinks by the riverbank.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: They don't do it anymore?

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: It's still going on. It's an annual event.

updateNotebook.memo: The Takashima Dance was once a festival that brought the whole village together.
updateNotebook.quote: In the old days, the whole village would gather for this dance.
updateNotebook.speaker: oldman

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Did you see the water grass flowing?

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Yes. The water was flowing steadily in one direction.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: That water will eventually flow into Lake Biwa, and then return to the sky.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: It falls as rain on the mountains, and comes back to this river.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: So the water is always circulating.

dialogs.speaker: oldman
dialogs.text: Water circulates. And people, too, will someday find their way back.

updateNotebook.memo: Water flows into Lake Biwa, becomes rain, and returns to the mountains.
updateNotebook.quote: Water circulates. And people, too, will someday find their way back.
updateNotebook.speaker: oldman
